messages:
ashok: Quick design note: propose a deferred enrichment path for mobile traces to reduce repeated late-enrich costs. Approach: batch un-enriched traces for a short window, emit a lightweight tombstone if a billing_key never resolves, and skip future enrich attempts until tombstone TTL expires.

sarah: Can you sketch the tradeoffs? worried about query fidelity + storage overhead :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ashok: Tradeoffs: compute saved vs extra storage & query complexity. Example: 2M mobile traces/day, 3% late-join -> naive re-enrich every 10m = many wasted lookups. Tombstones (16B key + 24B metadata) ~= tens of MBs for 24h across cluster; CPU savings can be significant.

tj: Query semantics question: if tombstone present and a user queries for billing breakdown, should we return "unknown" or trigger a backfill?

kevin: Two-tier semantics: "strong" flows (billing/chargebacks) cause backfill-on-read; "best-effort" flows (dashboards) use cohort heuristics that ignore tombstones. We need flags on queries.

maria: Operational details: how do we create and GC tombstones? race conditions possible if enrich arrives while tombstone writes.

ashok: Implementation sketch: a tiny kv table keyed by (tenant,billing_key_hash). Value: tombstone_version|created_ts|ttl. Tombstone write is conditional (only if no version or version < new). When a late enrich returns a billing_key, it issues a tombstone-delete with version > tombstone_version. Consumers check tombstone atomically before calling enrich.

tj: For correctness, tombstone writes should be monotonic. Use unsigned 64 bit version = epoch_ms at write-time. Deletes only succeed if version in tombstone <= delete_version. That avoids deletes lost to concurrent lower-version writes.

ashok: Consumer flow: 1) ingest fast-path accepts trace with missing billing_key and appends to short-lived window topic. 2) windowed consumer groups by billing_key_hash and tenant, checks tombstone kv, and calls enrich only for keys with no tombstone. 3) when window expires and no billing_key seen -> write tombstone with version=now and emit tombstone metric.

kevin: Config knobs: window_seconds (default 300), tombstone_ttl_seconds (default 86400), batch_size, backfill_on_read boolean. Make per-tenant overrides.

sarah: Metrics to add: enrichment.windowed.batch_size, enrichment.tombstone.created, enrichment.tombstone.expired, enrichment.tombstone.hit_rate, enrichment.backfill.invocations. Alerts: tombstone.hit_rate > 20% for 24h -> review.

maria: How do we handle late-arriving canonical billing_keys that arrive after tombstone creation? We delete tombstone; queries that read between tombstone and delete might see "unknown" temporarily. Document eventual consistency.

ashok: Exactly. We'll document: tombstone is a best-effort optimization for cost; it does not change long-term correctness because backfill-on-read or periodic backfills can rehydrate billing attribution.

ops-bot: scheduled: enrichment-deferred-canary -> rollout 2% traffic -> Tue 02:00 UTC

tj: Implementation tasks: (1) KV tombstone service (support TTL + conditional writes), (2) windowed consumer in late-enrich service, (3) query layer: opt-in backfill on read, (4) per-tenant config + feature flag, (5) dashboards + alerts.

kevin: Also need a cost-model doc: estimate compute saved vs storage & extra GC IO. I'll draft after we get canary numbers.

sarah: One more edge-case: what about multi-key normalization? mobile SDK may send different keys for same user -> we should normalize before tombstone keying, otherwise we might tombstone wrong namespace.

maria: Agree. Normalization step must run before grouping and tombstone checks. Otherwise we explode cases.

ashok: I'll open an RFC PR with the consumer pseudocode, tombstone KV API, and config knobs. Please comment on the PR with concerns about semantics and rollout plan. Thanks! :pray:
